steps.done: 84π = 263.9 cm³. The new move: split, then add.

steps.say: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height. Let us fill one in.

steps.pre: How many 1 cm cubes fill it?
steps.done: 40 cubes. That was the whole point: multiply all three lengths.

steps.say: Volume of a cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). The new move is that ⅓.

steps.done: V = 226.2 cm³. The new move: the ⅓ a cone always needs.

steps.pre: The bottom layer is 3 cubes long and 2 cubes deep. How many cubes in one layer? 3 × 2 =

steps.say: The box is 2 layers tall, so stack that layer up.

You just found a volume. Counting the cubes that fill a shape IS its volume, and the shortcut is length × width × height = 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 cm³. Every formula today (cylinders, cones, spheres) is just a cleverer way of counting the space inside.

steps: Choose the correct formula (given on the formula sheet for cones, spheres, pyramids)
Substitute measurements carefully (radius vs diameter, perpendicular height vs slant)
Calculate and give correct units (cm³ for volume, cm² for surface area)
method_card.title: Volume & Surface Area
method_card.content:
Prisms: Volume = area of cross-section × length. Cuboid: V = \(lwh\), SA = \(2(lw + lh + wh)\). Cylinder: V = \(\pi r^2 h\), SA = \(2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\).

Pyramid: V = \(\frac{1}{3} \times\) base area \(\times h\). Cone: V = \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\), Curved SA = \(\pi r l\) (\(l\) = slant height). Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), SA = \(4\pi r^2\).
method_card.example:
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm.

\(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \times 16 \times 10 = 160\pi \approx 502.7\) cm³

steps: Composite solid: split it into basic shapes, find each part, then add (joined) or subtract (a piece removed).
Keep each part in multiples of π until the final line, then round once.
Rearrange: to find a length from a given volume or area, substitute the known values and solve, cancelling π where you can.
gold.title: Gold: composite solids and rearranging formulae

example.question: A hemisphere has radius 3 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

steps: Cuboid: volume = length × width × height. Cube: volume = side³.
Prism: volume = cross-section area × length. Cylinder: volume = π r² h.
Surface area: add the area of every face. A cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh); a cube is 6 × side².
bronze.title: Bronze: volume and surface area of basic solids

example.question: Find the volume of a cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm.

steps: Cone: V = ⅓ π r² h. Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\) π r³, SA = 4 π r². Pyramid: V = ⅓ × base area × h.
A hemisphere is half a sphere, so halve the sphere volume.
Reverse: to find a missing length, put the numbers in and rearrange. Working in multiples of π keeps it exact.
silver.title: Silver: cones, spheres, pyramids and reverse problems

example.question: A cone has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

gold.hint: Total surface area of a cone is π r l (curved) plus π r² (base).
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cone has radius 3 cm and slant height 5 cm. Find the total surface area to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Total surface area of a cone is the curved part \(\pi r l\) plus the base \(\pi r^2\). Find each in π units.

misconceptions.message: Total surface area includes the base π r² as well as the curved part π r l: 15π + 9π = 24π = 75.4 cm². The curved surface alone is 47.1.

gold.hint: Big cone volume minus small cone volume. Work in multiples of π.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A frustum is formed by removing a small cone (r=2, h=3) from a large cone (r=6, h=9). Find the volume of the frustum to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: The frustum is the big cone with the small tip cone removed. Find each cone in π units, then subtract.

misconceptions.message: The tip is removed, so subtract: 108π − 4π = 104π = 326.7 cm³. Adding the cones gives 351.9.

gold.hint: The cylinder has radius 5 and height 10. Empty space = cylinder − sphere.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A sphere fits exactly inside a cylinder. The sphere has radius 5 cm. Find the volume of the empty space inside the cylinder. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: The sphere touches the cylinder all round, so the cylinder has radius 5 and height 10 (the diameter). Empty space = cylinder − sphere.

guided_steps.done: So the empty space is 261.8 cm³.

guided_steps.pre: Check: the gap is exactly a third of the cylinder, \(\frac{250\pi}{3}\) rounds to

misconceptions.message: That is the whole cylinder. The empty space is what is left after the sphere is removed: 250π − \(\frac{500\pi}{3}\) = \(\frac{250\pi}{3}\) = 261.8 cm³.

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A solid is a cylinder (r=4 cm, h=10 cm) with a hemisphere (r=4 cm) on top. Find the total volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Total volume = cylinder + hemisphere on top. Work each out as a decimal, then add.

guided_steps.pre: Check in π units: 160 + \(\frac{128}{3}\) = \(\frac{608}{3}\), and \(\frac{608\pi}{3}\) rounds to

misconceptions.message: The top is a HALF sphere: use ½ × \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\) = \(\frac{128\pi}{3}\) = 134.0 cm³, giving a total of 636.7 cm³. A full sphere on top gives 770.7.

gold.hint: Surface area of a sphere is 4πr². Set it equal to 100π; the π cancels.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A sphere has surface area \(100\pi\) cm². Find the radius.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a sphere is \(4\pi r^2\). Set it equal to 100π and the π cancels.

guided_steps.pre: Divide both sides by π: 100π ÷ π =
Check: 4 × π × 5² in π units is 4 × 25 =

misconceptions.message: 25 is r², not r. Take the square root: r = √25 = 5 cm.
Do not drop the 4: 100π = 4πr² gives r² = 25 and r = 5 cm, not r² = 100.

bronze.hint: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cuboid with length 6 cm, width 4 cm and height 3 cm.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height. Multiply all three.

misconceptions.message: 108 cm² is the surface area, 2(lw + lh + wh). Volume is l × w × h = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cm³.

bronze.hint: A cube has 6 identical square faces: find one, then times by 6.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the surface area of a cube with side length 5 cm.

guided_steps.say: A cube has 6 identical square faces. Find one face, then multiply by 6.

guided_steps.done: 125 is the volume; the surface area is 150 cm².

misconceptions.message: 125 cm³ is the volume (5³). Surface area = 6 × 5² = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

bronze.hint: Volume of any prism is the cross-section area times the length.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A triangular prism has a cross-section area of 12 cm² and length 10 cm. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of any prism is the cross-section area times the length.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 12 cm² cross-section, so V = 120 cm³.

misconceptions.message: Multiply, do not add: volume of a prism = cross-section area × length = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³.

bronze.hint: Volume of a cylinder is π r² h. Square the radius first.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cylinder is \(\pi r^2 h\). Square the radius first.

guided_steps.hint: Use the π button, round to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: π × 3² × 7 rounds to

misconceptions.message: The radius must be squared: V = π × 3² × 7 = 63π = 197.9 cm³, not π × 3 × 7.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cuboid has volume 180 cm³. Its length is 9 cm and width is 5 cm. Find the height.

guided_steps.say: Volume = length × width × height, so height = volume ÷ (length × width).

guided_steps.pre: Divide the volume by the base area: 180 ÷ 45 =

guided_steps.done: Back to 180 cm³, so h = 4 cm.

misconceptions.message: Divide by BOTH known lengths: height = 180 ÷ (9 × 5) = 180 ÷ 45 = 4 cm. Dividing by only the 9 gives 20.

bronze.hint: Volume of a cube is side × side × side.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cube with side length 4 cm.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cube is side × side × side.

guided_steps.pre: Compare: the surface area would be 6 × 16 =
guided_steps.done: 96 is the surface area; the volume is 64 cm³.

misconceptions.message: 96 cm² is the surface area (6 × 4²). Volume = 4³ = 64 cm³.

bronze.hint: The diameter is 10 cm, so halve it to get the radius first.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cylinder has diameter 10 cm and height 6 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: The diameter is 10 cm, so halve it to get the radius first.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: π × 5² × 6 rounds to

misconceptions.message: Halve the diameter first: radius = 5 cm, so V = π × 5² × 6 = 150π = 471.2 cm³. Using 10 as the radius gives 1885.0.

bronze.hint: Surface area of a cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh). Find the three different faces first.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the surface area of a cuboid 8 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh). Find the three different faces first.

guided_steps.hint: That is half the surface area.

misconceptions.message: 48 cm³ is the volume. Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(24 + 16 + 6) = 92 cm².

silver.hint: Volume of a cone is one third of π r² h.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cone has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Build the \(\pi r^2 h\) part, then take a third.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: ⅓ × π × 25 × 12 rounds to

misconceptions.message: That is the full cylinder. A cone is one third: V = ⅓ × π × 5² × 12 = 100π = 314.2 cm³.

silver.hint: Volume of a sphere is four thirds of π r³. Cube the radius first.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A sphere has radius 6 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a sphere is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Cube the radius first.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 216 rounds to

misconceptions.message: Cube the radius, do not square it: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 6³ = 288π = 904.8 cm³.

silver.hint: Surface area of a sphere is 4 π r². Square the radius first.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A sphere has radius 4 cm. Find the surface area to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a sphere is \(4\pi r^2\). Square the radius first.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: 4 × π × 4² rounds to

misconceptions.message: That is the volume. Surface area = 4 π r² = 4 × π × 4² = 64π = 201.1 cm².

silver.hint: Surface area of a cylinder is 2πr² + 2πrh. Work in multiples of π.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cylinder has surface area 150π cm². Its radius is 5 cm. Find its height.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a cylinder is \(2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h\). Work in multiples of π so it stays exact.

guided_steps.pre: The two circular ends are 2πr². In π units: 2 × 5² =
Take the ends off the total: 150 − 50 =
The curved part is 2πrh = 10πh, so 100 = 10h, h = 100 ÷ 10 =

misconceptions.message: Subtract the two circular ends first: 150π − 50π = 100π = 2πrh, giving h = 10 cm. Forgetting the ends gives 15.

silver.hint: Volume of a pyramid is one third of base area × height.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm. Find the volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a pyramid is \(\frac{1}{3} \times\) base area \(\times h\). Find the base area first.

misconceptions.message: That is base area × height with no third. A pyramid is one third: V = ⅓ × 36 × 10 = 120 cm³.

silver.hint: A hemisphere is half a sphere: find the full sphere, then halve it.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A hemisphere has radius 9 cm. Find its volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: A hemisphere is half a sphere. Find the full sphere's volume, then halve it.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: \(\frac{2}{3}\) × π × 729 rounds to

misconceptions.message: A hemisphere is HALF a sphere: V = ½ × \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 9³ = 486π = 1526.8 cm³. The full sphere (3053.6) is double.

silver.hint: Volume of a cone is ⅓πr²h. Work in multiples of π.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cone has volume 150π cm³ and radius 5 cm. Find the height.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Work in multiples of π to keep it exact.

guided_steps.pre: So ⅓ × 25 × h = 150. Multiply both sides by 3: 150 × 3 =

guided_steps.done: 150π, matching the given volume, so h = 18 cm.

misconceptions.message: Keep the ⅓: 150 = ⅓ × 25 × h gives 25h = 450 and h = 18 cm. Dropping the third gives 6.
